data.name: Darsh
data.gender_notes: Darsh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who sees, perceives, or understands the truth, reality, or wisdom. The name Darsh carries the meaning “Sight, Vision” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Darsh usually hope their child will grow to embody sight, vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who seek spiritual enlightenment and inner wisdom.
data.etymology: Darsh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sight, Vision.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darsh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the term "Darsh" holds immense importance, especially in the context of religious pilgrimages and visiting temples. Darshan, derived from the root word "Darsh," refers to the divine sight of seeing a deity or a Guru. It is believed that receiving the Darshan of a deity or a spiritual figure reinforces one's faith, bestows blessings, and brings inner peace.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Darsh represents the highest form of self-realization and understanding the truth or reality of the world, oneself, and the Divine. It underscores the importance of inner transformation and seeking wisdom rather than physical possessions or material wealth. The word Darsh carries an enlightening and transformative power, inspiring individuals to seek spiritual growth and pursue a path of wisdom and self-understanding.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Darsh in Hindu tradition represents the divine vision or the inner awakening to the truth and beauty of the universe. It symbolizes the realization that the Supreme Consciousness is present in all things and can be perceived through direct experience.

vedic_reference.note: Darsh is a common name for both boys and girls in Hinduism and also used as a title for religious leaders who lead the devotees towards the deity during puja or darshan.

historical_references.reference: Darsh, a Hindu monk and philosopher lived during the Gupta period (4th to 6th century CE) and is known for his philosophical works on Advaita Vedanta. He is also known as 'Jivanmukta Darshana', which means 'the knowledge of a living liberated soul'.

Darsh, a medieval Hindu king of the Yadava dynasty in the Deccan region of India, ruled during the late 13th and early 14th centuries CE. He is known for his patronage of literature, arts, and architecture, particularly the famous cave temples of Ellora and Ajanta.
